source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 1012 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1012 was established by Ordinance No. 31196, passed by the Dallas City Council on May 8, 2019. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1012 is established on property generally located along the west side of Stemmons Freeway Service Road, north of Viceroy Drive. The size of PD 1012 is approximately 20.99 acres. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) In this article:

(1) COMMUNITY RESOURCE CAMPUS means a mixed-use development with the primary purpose of providing programs, resources, assistance and shelter to at-risk, pre- homeless, and homeless individuals.

(2) DECLARED EMERGENCY means an event during which the governor or mayor has made an official declaration of emergency under Texas Government Code Section 418.014 or Dallas City Code Section 14B-6.

(3) DINING FACILITY means a facility for the preparation and service of food within a community resource campus that is limited to use by clients, employees, and volunteers of the community resource campus and is not open to the general public. A dining facility may include kitchen facilities as well as dining and wash rooms.

(4) EXTREME WEATHER CONDITIONS means any day during which at any time the wind chill is below 32 degrees Fahrenheit or the heat index is more than 100 degrees Fahrenheit.
(5) PERMANENT SUPPORTIVE HOUSING means a structure or group of structures with three or more dwelling units that are for seniors, ages 55 and older, or veterans of the United States armed services transitioning out of homelessness into permanent housing with access to social services at a community resource campus.

(6) TRANSITIONAL HOUSING means an interim residential facility that provides room and board to individuals or families transitioning from homelessness to long-term housing.

(d) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 1012A: conceptual plan. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 1012A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the IR Industrial/Research District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the IR Industrial/Research District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the IR Industrial/Research District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the IR Industrial/Research district is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following additional main uses are permitted by right:

-- Community resource campus.

(c) The following uses are permitted only in association with a community resource campus if the community resource campus includes two of the uses listed in Subsection (d):

-- Convalescent and nursing home, hospice care and related institutions. -- Dining facility. -- Overnight general purpose shelter. [The requirements in Section 51A-4.205 (2.1)(E)(v) do not apply.] -- Permanent supportive housing. -- Transitional housing.

(d) The uses listed in Subsection (c) are only permitted if two of the following uses are located on the Property in conjunction with a community resource campus:

-- Child-care facility. -- Church. -- Community service center. -- Indoor animal shelter or clinic without outside runs. -- Medical clinic or ambulatory surgical center. -- Office. -- Private recreation center, club, or area. -- Technical school. -- Warehouse. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.108. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for IR Industrial/Research District apply.

(b) Permanent supportive housing use in association with a community resource campus. The maximum number of dwelling units is 100. Permanent supportive housing units are limited to efficiencies or one-bedroom units.

(c) Floor area for transitional housing and overnight general purpose shelter. Single- bed sleeping quarters must have a minimum usable floor area of 125 square feet. Sleeping quarters containing two or more beds must have a minimum usable floor area that is equal to or greater than 60 square feet times the number of beds in the room. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general.

(1) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(2) The entire Property is considered one lot for parking purposes.
(b) Community resource campus.

(1) In order to qualify for the parking reductions in this subsection, a development plan must be approved by the city plan commission with a minimum of three allowable uses in a community resource campus. If the development plan is phased, the first

phase of the development plan must include a minimum of 100 parking spaces or the sum of required parking for the individual uses included in the first phase of the development plan, whichever is greater.

(2) The following parking ratios apply to a community resource campus complying with Paragraph (1).

(A) Church.

(i) One space per 10 seats up to a maximum of 300 seats is required. Parking for more than 300 seats must be provided at a ratio of one space per four seats for the seats over 300. If fixed benches or pews are provided, each 18 inches of length of the fixed bench or pews constitutes one fixed seat for purposes of this subparagraph.

(ii) If seating is not fixed, one space per 180 square feet is required for sanctuary or auditorium space less than 5,400 square feet in size. Parking for more than 5,400 square feet of sanctuary or auditorium space must be provided at a ratio of one space per 28 square feet for the area over 5,400 square feet.

(B) Community service center. One space per 500 square feet of floor area.

(C) Convalescent and nursing home, hospice care, and related institutions. None required.

(D) Office. One space per 500 square feet of floor area associated with a community resource campus is required.

(E) Other uses. Parking is not required for private recreation centers, dining facilities, classrooms, child care facilities, and animal shelters or clinics without outside runs that are accessible only to campus clients.

(F) Permanent supportive housing. One space per dwelling unit.

(G) Transitional housing and overnight general purpose shelter. One space per 3,000 square feet of transitional housing and overnight general purpose shelter facilities is required. Additional parking is not required during a declared emergency or extreme weather conditions.

(H) Warehouse. One space per 4,000 square feet of floor area is required. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this article, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Design Standards For A Community Resource
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.113. DESIGN STANDARDS FOR A COMMUNITY RESOURCE CAMPUS.

(a) Open space. A minimum of five percent of the total site area must be provided as open space. Open space may include recreational facilities available to residents of the site or unprogrammed green space with a minimum area of 10,000 square feet. Open space must be landscaped to include grass or other ground cover and may include sidewalks or other pedestrian facilities.

(b) Sidewalks.

(1) Sidewalks must be provided between all buildings and recreational facilities. Sidewalks must also be provided between any transit facility located on the perimeter of the site and the interior sidewalk system.

(2) Minimum sidewalk width is five feet.

(c) Fences.

(1) A minimum eight-foot masonry or decorative metal perimeter fence must be provided as shown in the conceptual plan.

(2) Chain-link fencing is prohibited. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.114. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) The entire Property is considered one lot for signage purposes. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) Maintenance. The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Compliance. Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) Community resource campus. For a community resource campus, the following additional provisions are required:

(1) Security. A minimum of four security personnel are required at all times. Except for the DART bus turn-around, all driveways along Viceroy Drive and Empress Row must be gated and secured. Office space must be provided for use by security personnel and law enforcement officers.

(2) Property owner engagement. The owner or operator of a community resource campus shall establish a community review committee to discuss problems and concerns, and to suggest improvements and changes if needed. This committee shall meet once every three months for the first year following the issuance of a certificate of occupancy for a residential use associated with a community service campus; and twice per year for the remaining lifetime of this use. Membership of the review committee should include one representative for each property owner within a 500-foot radius of the property.

(3) Driveway locations. The development plan for a community resource campus must include a deceleration lane for the main access and driveway on the Stemmons Freeway southbound frontage road pending review and approval by the Texas Department of Transportation. The southern driveway on Empress Row must be aligned with Titan Drive.

(4) Perimeter refuse collection. The owner or operator of a community resource campus shall provide for daily refuse collection around the perimeter of the site.

(5) Perimeter lighting. Perimeter lighting between the required fence and the street curb on Viceroy Drive and Empress Row must be provided with a minimum three foot- candle.

(6) Public entry. Public vehicular entry to a community resource campus is limited to the Stemmons Freeway driveways as shown on the conceptual plan. All visitors and clients must enter the campus through the community service center building in the location shown on the conceptual plan at a staffed and secure entrance to the campus.

(7) Maximum overnight guests in association with a community resource campus. The maximum number of overnight guests in transitional housing, convalescent and nursing home, hospice care and related institutions, and overnight general purpose shelters is 600 except during extreme weather conditions or declared emergencies. (Ord. 31196)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1012.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 31196)
